hints: Look at each of the four named structures and ask yourself, is it surrounded by a membrane at all?
Remember which organelle is just made of RNA and protein with no surrounding membrane, so it cannot be partially permeable.
walkthrough:
**Recall what partially permeable means**

Great start. A partially permeable membrane is a phospholipid membrane that controls what enters and leaves. So the question is really asking, which of these organelles are membrane-bound?

**Check 1, 2 and 3**

The Golgi apparatus is made of membrane-bound sacs and vesicles. The lysosome is a single membrane-bound sac holding enzymes. The mitochondrion has two membranes, an outer and a folded inner membrane. All three have partially permeable membranes.

**Check 4, the ribosome**

This is the odd one out. A ribosome is tiny, about 20 nm, and is made only of ribosomal RNA and protein. It has no membrane around it at all, so it cannot have a partially permeable membrane. That leaves 1, 2 and 3 only, which is option A.

options.A: Correct and well spotted. Golgi apparatus, lysosome and mitochondrion are all membrane-bound, so all have partially permeable membranes, while ribosome does not.
options.B: Not quite. This wrongly includes 4, the ribosome, which has no membrane at all, and it is only protein plus rRNA.
options.C: Almost, but this wrongly includes 4 and leaves out 2. Lysosome definitely has a single partially permeable membrane to contain its enzymes.
options.D: Close, but this wrongly includes 4 and leaves out 1. Golgi apparatus is made of membrane-bound cisternae and vesicles, so it must be included.
